statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 7, low, for the 01:00Z hour. The Sunday reopen has now produced a complete two-way round trip: after topping near 29,470.25-29,480.25 Nasdaq-100 futures sold roughly 145 to 175 points to 29,303.50-29,335.00 and have recovered to 29,405.50 (up 0.06%) at 01:04Z and 29,430.25 (up 0.14%) at 01:13Z on two independent sources, leaving price close to the 29,387.75 previous close and in the middle of its band. A pullback that was itself retraced is the opposite of the no-retracement path Tail measures, so Tail eases from 8 to 7. Stress is 38, moderate, down from 39: WTI has extended its decline to $84.98, down 2.39%, and Brent to $92.18, down 2.34%, on profit-taking ahead of the 18:00Z sanctions announcement, while long-end Treasury yields stay near multi-month highs with the 30-year at 5.23% and the 10-year at 4.69% on the 20 August H.15 and VIX sits at 14.89. Confidence is 86, high, on two independent live futures quotes covering a full observed round trip, a second index verified live, an official yield release, verified oil levels from two sources, complete delayed cross-asset context and a calendar confirmed against two independent feeds. The narrow 18:00Z-20:00Z danger window around the US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions is unchanged and Tail remains below the block threshold throughout the forecast.
recommendation: The observed reopen path is now positively consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than merely lacking evidence against it. Over the first three and a half hours of the Globex week Nasdaq-100 futures have printed a high, a decline of roughly 145 to 175 points, and a recovery of around 100 points back to the middle of the band. Both directions retraced. There is no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after a failed retracement and no session-extreme holding, which are the specific behaviours that have previously overwhelmed a reverse or grid approach. Cross-asset context agrees and is benign: S&P 500 futures are 7,701.75, up 0.14%, inside a 22-point band, delayed Treasury futures are flat to 0.14% firmer, VIX futures are 0.3% lower, gold is 0.14% lower and crude is more than 2% lower. Latest-session leadership is mixed rather than aligned, with five of eight megacaps higher but semiconductors averaging -0.70%, which caps directional conviction. The exposures that remain are cross-asset and scheduled. Long-end yields near multi-month highs keep bond volatility the main transmission channel into the Nasdaq-100, the 18:00Z US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions is the day's one high-impact catalyst, and Wednesday carries the PCE, GDP and durable-goods stack at 12:30Z together with Nvidia results after the close. Those raise Stress and shape the conditional path; none of them is observed price-path evidence, and none maps to a blocking Tail level at this time.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures complete a 145-175 point Asian round trip back to 29,405.50-29,430.25: Tail eases to 7, low, mapped policy state EA_ON, with conditional readings of 7 to 18 over the next twenty-three hours peaking at Monday's 18:00Z US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions.
body:
Three and a half hours into the Globex week the Sunday reopen has resolved into a contained, fully two-way price path. Nasdaq-100 futures topped near 29,470.25-29,480.25, sold roughly 145 to 175 points to a session low of 29,303.50 on one source and 29,335.00 on another, and have recovered to 29,405.50, up 17.75 points and 0.06%, at 01:04Z and 29,430.25, up 42.50 and 0.14%, at 01:13Z. Against the 29,387.75 previous close and the 29,388.50 reopen print that leaves the contract effectively flat in the middle of a band roughly 145 to 177 points wide. The important change from the previous hour is not the level but the structure: the first meaningful pullback of the week occurred and was itself retraced, which is the behaviour a reverse or grid approach depends on.

S&P 500 futures are 7,701.75, up 10.50 and 0.14%, at 01:12Z inside a much narrower 7,681.50-7,703.25 range, so the pullback was tech-led and did not propagate into the broad index. That is a normal leadership rotation pattern rather than a dislocation. The most recent Nasdaq-100 cash close was 29,995.38, down 0.17%, near the low of a 29,971.92-30,195.72 range, on a day when the S&P 500 rose 0.4% to 7,674.37 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4% to 26,180.45 while finishing the week down 2.1%. Megacap drag against a broad advance is corroborated by the latest-session sector picture: software up 1.15% to 1.18%, communication services up 0.92%, but semiconductors down 0.31% and semiconductor equipment up only 0.05%.

Delayed cross-asset context is consistent and benign. Nasdaq futures 0.27%, S&P futures 0.12%, Dow futures 0.02%, VIX futures -0.3%, gold -0.14%, and two-, five-, ten- and thirty-year Treasury futures flat to 0.14% firmer, so the marginal overnight move in duration is small yield relief rather than another leg higher. Crude has extended its decline: WTI is $84.98, down 2.39%, and Brent $92.18, down 2.34%, with Reuters reporting profit-taking ahead of the Treasury announcement after both contracts posted a second consecutive weekly gain of more than 5%. Falling oil into a sanctions headline is a partial pre-discount, and it loosens rather than tightens the inflation channel into duration. VIX is 14.89, down 6.00%, a subdued level that sits awkwardly with the size of the week's scheduled stack but which no live evidence currently contradicts.

The rates backdrop remains the main structural exposure. The 20 August H.15 shows the two-year at 4.19%, the ten-year at 4.69% and the thirty-year at 5.23%, with the long end near multi-month highs after a tumultuous week for Treasurys and an unusual Treasury buyback intervention. This week brings $69 billion of two-year notes on Tuesday, $70 billion of five-year notes on Wednesday and $44 billion of seven-year notes on Thursday, so a long-end auction tail is the most plausible route from rates into Nasdaq-100 structure.

Geopolitics is an ongoing, largely priced condition rather than a fresh discontinuity. The Strait of Hormuz remains essentially shut, having previously carried about a fifth of global seaborne oil, and indirect US-Iran contacts continue. The scheduled step is the 18:00Z Treasury news conference at which the Secretary has threatened the toughest sanctions in history. No new escalation has been verified in the last hour.

On the calibration that matters, Tail measures the pathological price path that denies mean reversion long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach. The current hour supplies direct contrary evidence in the form of a completed round trip, so Tail is 7. Stress at 38 carries the scheduled sanctions announcement, elevated long-end yields, heavy coupon supply and Wednesday's PCE and Nvidia stack. Confidence at 86 reflects two independent live futures quotes spanning an observed structure, a second index verified live, an official yield release, oil verified from two sources and a calendar cross-checked against two independent feeds.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past twenty-four hours is nearly complete: twenty hourly assessments are available and four clock-hours are marked unavailable, at 07:00Z, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z on 23 August. Tail held 4 through every hour of the weekend futures halt, when no Nasdaq-100 price path could develop at all, stepped to 15 in the 22:00Z reopen hour to cover the still-unpriced weekend queue, then fell back to 9 at 23:00Z and 8 at 00:00Z once the reopen printed without a gap. The mapped policy state stayed EA_ON and the dominant mode remained normal in every available hour, so no hour approached the block threshold. Stress traced a full weekend arc: 37 at the start of the window, a low of 34 through the European morning and early afternoon, then a steady climb across the evening to 45 in the last three pre-reopen hours as the tariff escalation and Monday's scheduled Iran announcement accumulated, before easing to 42 and then 39 once the reopen cleared. Confidence sat between 82 and 87 throughout, dipping to its low of 82 in the reopen hour when the first live print was still incomplete and recovering to 86 immediately afterwards.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail 7 and Stress 38 on an observed round trip rather than on assumption: two independent verified quotes now cover a high, a 145 to 175 point decline and a recovery back to mid-range inside the Asian session. Conditional Tail then holds a floor of 7 through the quietest Asian hours, where two-way trade has historically been most reliable and no US release is scheduled, while Stress decays to 36 as the weekend risk premium finishes unwinding. Tail steps to 9 for the European pre-open and 11 at the 07:00Z European cash open, the first substantial liquidity event and the point at which any overnight drift is confirmed or faded, then eases again through a quiet European late morning. The 12:30Z Chicago Fed National Activity Index is treated as a checkpoint at Tail 11 rather than a step, because it is a medium-impact composite. The US cash open inside the 13:00Z hour carries 15 for opening-auction continuation risk, easing to 14 and 12 across the auction window and to 11 in the midday lull. The path peaks at 18 with Stress 49 and mode event/whipsaw for the 18:00Z and 19:00Z hours around the US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions, covering both the initial repricing and a delayed second leg through the question-and-answer session, then decays to 14 at the 20:00Z cash close and back to 8 by Tuesday's Asian session. Every forecast hour maps to EA_ON, because none reaches the block threshold on conditional risk alone. Confidence declines from 86 to 73 across the window purely with forecast distance from the last verified price observation, not because of conflicting evidence.
